governments.name: City of Nanaimo
governments.howBuilt: This list draws on reporting from the 2026 Nanaimo all-candidates forum, candidate statements compiled by local news outlets, the City of Nanaimo's 2026 budget and tax decisions, the 2026 local homelessness count, and a candidate survey on climate. We kept issues the City of Nanaimo can act on through zoning, its budget, bylaws, streets, and services. Issues mainly run by the province, such as health care, are left out of this list.

issues.title: Housing costs and supply
issues.description: How much housing gets built in Nanaimo, what kinds, where it goes, and how affordable it is to rent or buy.
issues.whatItAffects: Renters, first-time buyers, seniors, families, and workers looking for a place to live.
issues.whoDecides: Council sets zoning, approves building permits and development fees, and can offer city land or incentives for affordable units.

viewQuestion.question: How should the city approach new housing?
viewQuestion.poleA: Approve more homes faster, including taller and denser buildings
viewQuestion.poleB: Grow more gradually and protect the feel of existing neighbourhoods

issues.title: Community safety and street disorder
issues.description: How safe people feel downtown and in neighbourhoods, including crime, vandalism, and public drug use.
issues.whatItAffects: Residents, business owners, visitors, and people living on the street.
issues.whoDecides: Council funds the local RCMP detachment and bylaw officers, and decides how much to spend on enforcement versus outreach programs.

viewQuestion.question: Where should the city put more of its safety budget?
viewQuestion.poleA: More police and bylaw officers on patrol
viewQuestion.poleB: More outreach workers and community-based programs

issues.title: Homelessness and shelter
issues.description: How the city responds to people without a home, including shelters, supportive housing sites, and camping in public spaces.
issues.whatItAffects: People who are unhoused, nearby residents and businesses, and users of parks and public spaces.
issues.whoDecides: Council approves sites and zoning for shelters and supportive housing, sets rules for public spaces, and partners with BC Housing.

viewQuestion.question: What should the city focus on?
viewQuestion.poleA: Add more shelter and supportive housing sites across the city
viewQuestion.poleB: Set firmer limits on where people can shelter and camp

issues.title: Property taxes and city spending
issues.description: How much the city collects in property taxes and user fees each year, and what that money pays for.
issues.whatItAffects: Homeowners, renters through their rent, businesses, and everyone who uses city services.
issues.whoDecides: Council sets the yearly budget and tax rate, and decides which services and projects to fund, delay, or cut.

viewQuestion.question: How should the city balance its budget?
viewQuestion.poleA: Keep tax increases low, even if some services or projects wait
viewQuestion.poleB: Keep investing in services and projects, even if taxes rise more

issues.title: Downtown and waterfront
issues.description: The health of downtown Nanaimo and the waterfront, including empty storefronts, events, public spaces, and new development.
issues.whatItAffects: Downtown businesses, residents, workers, visitors, and people who use the waterfront.
issues.whoDecides: Council plans and funds public spaces, sets downtown zoning, runs events and permits, and can partner on waterfront projects.

viewQuestion.question: What should the city prioritize downtown?
viewQuestion.poleA: Use public money to lead projects and draw people downtown
viewQuestion.poleB: Keep public spending modest and let private investment lead

issues.title: Permit and approval times
issues.description: How long it takes to get city approval to build, renovate, or open a business, and how clear the rules are.
issues.whatItAffects: Home builders, small businesses, homeowners doing renovations, and people waiting for new housing.
issues.whoDecides: Council sets permit rules and fees, funds city planning staff, and decides how much review each project needs.

viewQuestion.question: What matters more in city approvals?
viewQuestion.poleA: Speed and simpler rules so projects can move ahead
viewQuestion.poleB: Careful review and public input, even if it takes longer

issues.title: Roads, water and sewer
issues.description: The condition of streets, sidewalks, water pipes, and sewers, and whether they can keep up as the city grows.
issues.whatItAffects: Every household and business that relies on clean water, working sewers, and safe roads.
issues.whoDecides: Council plans and pays for repairs and upgrades, and sets fees that new development pays toward them.

viewQuestion.question: How should the city pay for upkeep and upgrades?
viewQuestion.poleA: Spend more now to fix aging systems before they fail
viewQuestion.poleB: Spread repairs out over time to limit costs each year

issues.title: Getting around the city
issues.description: How people travel in Nanaimo by car, bus, bike, or on foot, including traffic, parking, and street safety.
issues.whatItAffects: Drivers, bus riders, cyclists, people walking, and anyone who can't drive.
issues.whoDecides: Council designs and maintains city streets, bike lanes, and sidewalks, and helps set bus service through the regional district.

viewQuestion.question: How should street space and money be shared?
viewQuestion.poleA: Focus on roads, traffic flow, and parking for drivers
viewQuestion.poleB: Shift more toward buses, bike lanes, and walking routes

issues.title: Trees, climate and natural areas
issues.description: How the city protects trees, green space, and natural areas, and prepares for heat, drought, and storms.
issues.whatItAffects: Residents, wildlife, parks users, and landowners whose property has trees or natural areas.
issues.whoDecides: Council sets tree protection and green building rules, buys and manages parkland, and plans for climate risks.

viewQuestion.question: How should the city balance growth and nature?
viewQuestion.poleA: Stronger rules to protect trees and natural areas
viewQuestion.poleB: More flexibility so landowners and builders can use land

governments.name: City of Victoria
governments.howBuilt: This list draws on candidate profiles and local news coverage of the 2026 Victoria election, the City of Victoria's 2023-2026 Strategic Plan and 2026 budget decisions, reporting on the Crystal Pool replacement, and the non-binding Victoria-Saanich amalgamation question on the 2026 ballot. We kept issues the City of Victoria can act on through zoning, its budget, bylaws, streets, and services.

issues.title: Housing costs and supply
issues.description: How much housing gets built in Victoria, what kinds, where it goes, and how affordable it is to rent or buy.
issues.whatItAffects: Renters, first-time buyers, students, seniors, families, and workers.
issues.whoDecides: Council sets zoning and density rules, approves development permits, and can require or fund affordable units.

viewQuestion.question: How should the city approach new housing?
viewQuestion.poleA: Approve more homes faster, including taller and denser buildings
viewQuestion.poleB: Grow more gradually and protect the feel of existing neighbourhoods

issues.title: Community safety and street disorder
issues.description: How safe people feel downtown and in neighbourhoods, including crime, vandalism, and public drug use.
issues.whatItAffects: Residents, business owners, visitors, and people living on the street.
issues.whoDecides: Council shares police funding with Esquimalt, funds bylaw officers, and decides how much to spend on enforcement versus outreach.

viewQuestion.question: Where should the city put more of its safety budget?
viewQuestion.poleA: More police and bylaw officers on patrol
viewQuestion.poleB: More outreach workers and non-police crisis teams

issues.title: Homelessness and sheltering
issues.description: How the city responds to people without a home, including shelters, supportive housing, and sheltering in parks.
issues.whatItAffects: People who are unhoused, nearby residents and businesses, and park users.
issues.whoDecides: Council sets rules for sheltering in parks and public spaces, approves sites for housing, and partners with the province.

viewQuestion.question: What should the city focus on?
viewQuestion.poleA: Add more shelter and supportive housing sites across the city
viewQuestion.poleB: Set firmer limits on sheltering in parks and public spaces

issues.title: Property taxes and city spending
issues.description: How much the city collects in property taxes each year, and how that money is spent across services.
issues.whatItAffects: Homeowners, renters through their rent, businesses, and everyone who uses city services.
issues.whoDecides: Council sets the yearly budget and tax rate, and decides which services and projects to fund, delay, or cut.

viewQuestion.question: How should the city balance its budget?
viewQuestion.poleA: Keep tax increases low, even if some services or projects wait
viewQuestion.poleB: Keep investing in services and projects, even if taxes rise more

issues.title: Downtown and local business
issues.description: The health of downtown Victoria, including empty storefronts, cleanliness, events, and how easy it is to run a business.
issues.whatItAffects: Downtown businesses and workers, residents, and visitors.
issues.whoDecides: Council sets downtown zoning, business licences and permits, funds street cleaning and public spaces, and supports events.

viewQuestion.question: What should the city prioritize downtown?
viewQuestion.poleA: Cleaner streets and more enforcement to bring people back
viewQuestion.poleB: More events, housing, and public spaces to bring people back

issues.title: Streets, cycling, transit and parking
issues.description: How people travel in Victoria by car, bus, bike, or on foot, including bike lanes, parking, and street safety.
issues.whatItAffects: Drivers, bus riders, cyclists, people walking, and businesses that rely on parking.
issues.whoDecides: Council designs city streets, bike lanes, and parking rules, and works with BC Transit on bus routes.

viewQuestion.question: How should street space and money be shared?
viewQuestion.poleA: Focus on traffic flow and parking for drivers
viewQuestion.poleB: Shift more toward buses, bike lanes, and walking routes

issues.title: Victoria and Saanich amalgamation
issues.description: Whether Victoria and Saanich should study becoming one municipality; a non-binding question is on the 2026 ballot.
issues.whatItAffects: Residents and businesses in both cities, city services, taxes, and local representation.
issues.whoDecides: Council can study the idea and ask voters, but a binding merger needs provincial approval and a later vote.

viewQuestion.question: What is your view on combining the two cities?
viewQuestion.poleA: Explore merging to share services and plan the region together
viewQuestion.poleB: Stay separate to keep local control and a distinct identity

issues.title: Climate and tree canopy
issues.description: How the city protects trees and green space, cuts emissions, and prepares for heat, drought, and storms.
issues.whatItAffects: Residents, parks users, property owners, and builders.
issues.whoDecides: Council sets tree protection and building rules, manages parks and city trees, and funds climate projects.

viewQuestion.question: How should the city balance growth and nature?
viewQuestion.poleA: Stronger rules to protect trees and act on climate
viewQuestion.poleB: More flexibility so housing and projects cost less

issues.title: Recreation and community facilities
issues.description: The state of pools, rec centres, parks, and arts spaces, including the Crystal Pool replacement.
issues.whatItAffects: Families, seniors, youth sports, arts groups, and anyone who uses public facilities.
issues.whoDecides: Council decides which facilities to build, fix, or replace, and how much to charge for programs.

viewQuestion.question: How should the city invest in facilities?
viewQuestion.poleA: Build or replace major facilities, even at a high cost
viewQuestion.poleB: Maintain what exists and keep costs down

issues.title: Relations with Lekwungen nations
issues.description: How the city works with the Songhees and Xwsepsum (Esquimalt) Nations on land, heritage, and shared decisions.
issues.whatItAffects: First Nations communities, city planning, heritage sites, and public spaces.
issues.whoDecides: Council sets city policy on partnerships, naming, heritage, and land use, and can make agreements with local nations.

viewQuestion.question: How should the city approach this work?
viewQuestion.poleA: Expand shared decision-making with local nations
viewQuestion.poleB: Keep decisions mainly with elected council

governments.name: School District 68 (Nanaimo-Ladysmith)
governments.howBuilt: This list draws on Nanaimo Ladysmith Public Schools' 2026-27 budget consultation and preliminary budget, local news on enrolment, child care, and the bid to replace Nanaimo District Secondary School, and coverage of the 2026 trustee election. We kept issues the school board can act on through its budget, policies, programs, and advocacy to the province.

issues.title: Aging school buildings
issues.description: The condition of older schools, including the push to replace the 74-year-old Nanaimo District Secondary School.
issues.whatItAffects: Students, staff, and families at older schools, and neighbourhoods around them.
issues.whoDecides: The board sets building priorities and asks the province for capital money; the province decides which projects get funded.

viewQuestion.question: How should the district approach older schools?
viewQuestion.poleA: Push hard for full replacements of the oldest schools
viewQuestion.poleB: Upgrade existing schools to spread money further

issues.title: District budget and enrolment
issues.description: How the district spends its budget as student numbers dip, including staffing and possible service reductions.
issues.whatItAffects: Students, teachers, support staff, and school programs across the district.
issues.whoDecides: The board approves the yearly budget and decides where to add or cut; most funding comes from the province per student.

viewQuestion.question: Where should the district protect spending?
viewQuestion.poleA: Protect classroom staff and programs, even if reserves shrink
viewQuestion.poleB: Keep reserves and reduce costs to match fewer students

issues.title: Before- and after-school care
issues.description: Whether schools offer child care before and after class, and how many spaces are available.
issues.whatItAffects: Working parents, young students, and school support staff.
issues.whoDecides: The board decides whether to run or host child care in schools; the province funds many new spaces.

viewQuestion.question: What role should schools play in child care?
viewQuestion.poleA: Schools should run more child care directly
viewQuestion.poleB: Schools should focus on learning and let others run child care

issues.title: Reading and math skills
issues.description: How well students are learning to read, write, and do math, and how the district tracks progress.
issues.whatItAffects: Students at every grade, teachers, and families.
issues.whoDecides: The board sets district learning goals, chooses supports and training, and decides how to measure results.

viewQuestion.question: How should the district improve learning?
viewQuestion.poleA: More testing and data to track each student's progress
viewQuestion.poleB: More teacher judgment and less focus on testing

issues.title: Student and staff well-being
issues.description: Mental health and well-being of students and staff, including counselling and support in schools.
issues.whatItAffects: Students, teachers, support staff, and families.
issues.whoDecides: The board decides how many counsellors and support staff to fund and which wellness programs to run.

viewQuestion.question: How should the district support well-being?
viewQuestion.poleA: Add more counsellors and wellness staff in schools
viewQuestion.poleB: Keep the focus on core teaching and refer out for support

issues.title: Support for diverse learners
issues.description: Help for students with disabilities or extra learning needs, including education assistants in classrooms.
issues.whatItAffects: Students with diverse needs, their classmates, teachers, and education assistants.
issues.whoDecides: The board decides how many education assistants and specialists to fund beyond what the province provides.

viewQuestion.question: How should the district support diverse learners?
viewQuestion.poleA: More students learning in regular classes with extra staff
viewQuestion.poleB: More specialized programs and spaces for students who need them

issues.title: Indigenous learning and relationships
issues.description: How schools include Indigenous history and culture and work with local First Nations, including Snuneymuxw and Stz'uminus.
issues.whatItAffects: Indigenous students and families, all students, and local First Nations.
issues.whoDecides: The board sets district goals, funds programs and staff, and makes agreements with local nations.

viewQuestion.question: How much focus should this get?
viewQuestion.poleA: Expand Indigenous learning across all subjects and schools
viewQuestion.poleB: Keep it as one part of a broad core curriculum

issues.title: Advocacy to the province
issues.description: How the board makes its case to the province for funding, new schools, and changes to the funding formula.
issues.whatItAffects: Students and families who depend on provincial decisions about local schools.
issues.whoDecides: Trustees can lobby MLAs and ministers and speak publicly, but the province controls most school funding.

viewQuestion.question: How should trustees deal with the province?
viewQuestion.poleA: Push publicly and firmly for more funding
viewQuestion.poleB: Work quietly with the province and manage within current funding

governments.name: School District 61 (Greater Victoria)
governments.howBuilt: This list draws on news coverage of the board's 2025 removal and 2026 reinstatement, the board's 2026-27 budget decisions, district updates on seismic and building projects, the new trustee electoral areas, and coverage of 2026 trustee candidates. We kept issues the school board can act on through its budget, policies, programs, and requests to the province.

issues.title: Board governance and accountability
issues.description: How the school board runs after trustees were removed by the province in 2025 and reinstated in 2026.
issues.whatItAffects: Families, staff, and taxpayers who rely on a stable, accountable board.
issues.whoDecides: Trustees set board rules, meeting practices, and how they report to the public and work with the province.

viewQuestion.question: What matters most for the next board?
viewQuestion.poleA: Independence to make local choices, even if the province disagrees
viewQuestion.poleB: Close cooperation with the province to avoid future conflict

issues.title: Budget and program choices
issues.description: How the district balances its budget and which programs, like middle school music and kindergarten educators, it keeps.
issues.whatItAffects: Students, families, teachers, and support staff.
issues.whoDecides: The board approves the yearly budget and decides which programs to fund, reduce, or cut within provincial funding.

viewQuestion.question: When money is tight, what should the district do?
viewQuestion.poleA: Protect student programs and cut administration or use reserves
viewQuestion.poleB: Make program changes to keep a balanced budget and reserves

issues.title: Police presence in schools
issues.description: Whether police liaison officers work in schools, and how student contact with police is tracked and reported.
issues.whatItAffects: Students, staff, families, and local police.
issues.whoDecides: The board decides whether to invite police liaison programs and sets reporting rules for school safety.

viewQuestion.question: What role should police have in schools?
viewQuestion.poleA: Bring back regular police liaison officers in schools
viewQuestion.poleB: Rely mainly on counsellors and staff, with police only when needed

issues.title: School building safety and space
issues.description: Earthquake upgrades, school replacements, and having enough classroom space as neighbourhoods change.
issues.whatItAffects: Students and staff in older schools, and families in growing neighbourhoods.
issues.whoDecides: The board sets building priorities and asks the province for capital funding; the province approves major projects.

viewQuestion.question: How should the district plan school buildings?
viewQuestion.poleA: Push for full replacements and expansions of older schools
viewQuestion.poleB: Upgrade existing schools to spread money further

issues.title: Trustee electoral areas
issues.description: The new system where trustees are elected by area instead of district-wide, used for the first time in 2026.
issues.whatItAffects: Voters in Victoria, Oak Bay, Saanich, Esquimalt, View Royal, and the Highlands.
issues.whoDecides: The board proposes the voting system for trustees, and the province must approve changes.

viewQuestion.question: How should trustees be elected?
viewQuestion.poleA: By area, so each community has its own trustee
viewQuestion.poleB: District-wide, so every trustee answers to all voters

issues.title: Early learning and child care
issues.description: Supports for young learners, like early childhood educators in kindergarten, and child care on school sites.
issues.whatItAffects: Kindergarten students, young families, and early childhood staff.
issues.whoDecides: The board decides whether to fund early learning staff and host child care; the province funds many spaces.

viewQuestion.question: What role should schools play in early learning?
viewQuestion.poleA: Expand early learning staff and child care in schools
viewQuestion.poleB: Focus district money on core K-12 teaching

issues.title: Support for diverse learners
issues.description: Help for students with disabilities or extra learning needs, including education assistants and specialists.
issues.whatItAffects: Students with diverse needs, their classmates, teachers, and education assistants.
issues.whoDecides: The board decides how many education assistants and specialists to fund beyond what the province provides.

viewQuestion.question: How should the district support diverse learners?
viewQuestion.poleA: More students learning in regular classes with extra staff
viewQuestion.poleB: More specialized programs and spaces for students who need them

issues.title: Use of school land
issues.description: Whether the district keeps, leases, or sells school land and buildings it is not using right now.
issues.whatItAffects: Families, neighbours of school sites, and future students in growing areas.
issues.whoDecides: The board decides whether to keep, lease, or sell district land, with provincial approval for sales.

viewQuestion.question: What should the district do with unused land?
viewQuestion.poleA: Keep land for future schools and community use
viewQuestion.poleB: Lease or sell some land to fund current needs

governments.name: Province of British Columbia
governments.howBuilt: This list draws on public opinion polling at the start of the 2026 provincial campaign, news coverage of party announcements and leaders' debates, and reporting on court rulings about B.C.'s Indigenous rights law. We kept issues the Province of British Columbia is responsible for, such as health care, provincial taxes, housing rules, justice, and K-12 funding.

issues.title: Cost of living
issues.description: The rising cost of everyday things like groceries, gas, hydro, insurance, and child care.
issues.whatItAffects: Households across B.C., especially those on low or fixed incomes.
issues.whoDecides: The province sets provincial taxes, rebates, ICBC and BC Hydro rates, child care fees, and minimum wage.

viewQuestion.question: What is the better way to ease costs?
viewQuestion.poleA: Lower taxes and fees so people keep more of their money
viewQuestion.poleB: Fund public programs and rebates that lower costs directly

issues.title: Health care access
issues.description: Finding a family doctor, wait times for surgery and emergency care, and staffing at hospitals and clinics.
issues.whatItAffects: Patients, families, seniors, and health care workers across B.C.
issues.whoDecides: The province runs and funds the health system, including hospitals, health authorities, doctor pay, and training spots.

viewQuestion.question: How should the province improve access?
viewQuestion.poleA: Expand public hospitals, clinics, and staff
viewQuestion.poleB: Allow more private and contracted options within public coverage

issues.title: Housing affordability
issues.description: The cost of renting and buying a home in B.C., and how many homes are being built.
issues.whatItAffects: Renters, buyers, landlords, builders, and young people starting out.
issues.whoDecides: The province sets rules for cities on zoning, funds affordable housing, sets tenancy rules, and charges property-related taxes.

viewQuestion.question: What should the province focus on?
viewQuestion.poleA: Require cities to approve more homes and fund public housing
viewQuestion.poleB: Cut taxes and red tape so private builders can build more

issues.title: Jobs and the economy
issues.description: The strength of B.C.'s economy, including jobs, wages, trade, and growth in different industries.
issues.whatItAffects: Workers, employers, and communities that depend on local industries.
issues.whoDecides: The province sets business taxes and rules, approves major projects, and funds job training.

viewQuestion.question: How should the province grow the economy?
viewQuestion.poleA: Speed up approvals and support major resource projects
viewQuestion.poleB: Invest in new industries and worker training

issues.title: Provincial deficit and spending
issues.description: The gap between what the province spends and what it takes in, and how quickly to close it.
issues.whatItAffects: Taxpayers, public services, and future generations who pay down debt.
issues.whoDecides: The province sets its budget, taxes, and spending levels across all ministries.

viewQuestion.question: How should the province handle the deficit?
viewQuestion.poleA: Cut spending to balance the budget sooner
viewQuestion.poleB: Keep funding services and balance the budget more slowly

issues.title: Crime and public safety
issues.description: Street crime, repeat offending, and how safe people feel in their communities.
issues.whatItAffects: Residents, business owners, victims of crime, and people in the justice system.
issues.whoDecides: The province funds RCMP policing in many areas, runs prosecutions and jails, and sets provincial safety laws.

viewQuestion.question: Where should the province focus?
viewQuestion.poleA: Tougher enforcement and more police
viewQuestion.poleB: More prevention, treatment, and social supports

issues.title: Addictions and mental health care
issues.description: Toxic drug deaths, addiction treatment, mental health services, and care for people in crisis.
issues.whatItAffects: People who use drugs, people with mental illness, their families, and communities.
issues.whoDecides: The province funds treatment and mental health services and sets rules on drug policy and involuntary care.

viewQuestion.question: What should the province emphasize?
viewQuestion.poleA: More treatment beds, including involuntary care in some cases
viewQuestion.poleB: More voluntary services and harm reduction

issues.title: Indigenous rights and land decisions
issues.description: How B.C. applies its law on Indigenous rights, after court rulings on land title and consultation.
issues.whatItAffects: First Nations, landowners, resource industries, and communities across B.C.
issues.whoDecides: The province can amend or keep its Indigenous rights law, negotiate agreements, and set land and resource rules.

viewQuestion.question: What should the province prioritize?
viewQuestion.poleA: Keep the law and share more decisions with First Nations
viewQuestion.poleB: Change the law to give more certainty to landowners and industry

issues.title: Resources and the environment
issues.description: How B.C. balances mining, forestry, and energy projects with protecting land, water, and the climate.
issues.whatItAffects: Resource workers, rural towns, First Nations, and everyone affected by climate and wildfires.
issues.whoDecides: The province approves resource projects, sets environmental rules, manages forests, and sets climate policy.

viewQuestion.question: How should the province balance these goals?
viewQuestion.poleA: Grow resource industries with fewer delays
viewQuestion.poleB: Stronger protections for land, water, and climate

issues.title: School funding and space
issues.description: How much the province spends on K-12 schools, and how it funds new and replacement schools.
issues.whatItAffects: Students, teachers, families, and school districts like Nanaimo-Ladysmith and Greater Victoria.
issues.whoDecides: The province sets the school funding formula, approves capital projects, and sets curriculum and class size rules.

viewQuestion.question: Where should new school money go first?
viewQuestion.poleA: New and replacement school buildings
viewQuestion.poleB: More teachers and supports in classrooms
